what: ENIAC ran its first real program (Los Alamos problem, likely thermonuclear calculations) at the Moore School, University of Pennsylvania

sources.title: December 1945: The ENIAC Computer Runs Its First, Top-Secret Program

what: Vannevar Bush and colleagues at MIT completed the operational mechanical Differential Analyzer
Herman Hollerith's punched-card tabulating machines used to tabulate the 1890 US Census
MIT demonstrated a Cincinnati Hydrotel milling machine driven by pre-punched tape (numerical control), for Parsons Corporation/US Air Force
Jack Kilby demonstrated the first working integrated circuit (germanium) to managers at Texas Instruments, Dallas
IBM announced the 305 RAMAC with the 350 disk storage unit, first commercial moving-head magnetic disk system, with units already installed at the US Navy and companies

sources.title: The IBM 305 RAMAC, the First Computer with a Hard Drive

what: John Benjamin Dancer in England made the first microphotographs (documents reduced to microscopic size)
Eastman Kodak bought George McCarthy's Checkograph and marketed it as Recordak, microfilming bank checks

sources.title: George McCarthy Invents the Checkograph, the First Commercial Application of Microfilm

what: Frank Rosenblatt's Perceptron (Cornell Aeronautical Lab, Navy-funded) demonstrated learning; 1958 Navy press event (IBM 704 simulation, Mark I hardware followed; sources disagree on exact public demo date, 1958 vs 1960)
Leonard Adleman solved a seven-node Hamiltonian path problem with DNA molecules in the lab (Science, Nov 1994)
Bowmar 901B, early pocket-size LED electronic calculator built on a TI chip, sold to consumers (introduction year 1971 vs 1972 disputed)

sources.title: The Consumer Electronics Hall of Fame: Bowmar 901B

what: MITS Altair 8800 kit computer on the cover of Popular Electronics, sold to individuals (about 2,000 in first month)
Apple II, Commodore PET and TRS-80 launched as ready-to-use home computers sold to the public
Psion Organiser, handheld pocket computer with diary/database, launched in the UK (Organiser II 1986 is often called the first usable PDA)

sources.title: Tales In Tech History: Psion Organiser

what: Palm Computing's PalmPilot, introduced March 1996, made PDAs a consumer must-have
CDC 6600 (Seymour Cray, released 1964), generally considered the first successful supercomputer, delivered to Livermore and Los Alamos; Manchester Atlas (Dec 1962) is an earlier contender
ENIAC ran the first computerized Monte Carlo simulations, of neutron diffusion in fission weapons, for Los Alamos (March-May 1948)

sources.title: Hitting the jackpot: the birth of the Monte Carlo method
Los Alamos Bets on ENIAC: Nuclear Monte Carlo Simulations, 1947-1948

what: Ivan Sutherland's Sketchpad at MIT, generally recognized as the first computer-aided drafting program (running by 1961 in earlier form)

sources.title: Ivan Sutherland demonstrating Sketchpad on the TX-2

what: Robot Scientist Adam (Aberystwyth/Cambridge, Ross King) autonomously generated and experimentally tested hypotheses about yeast genes, confirmed by humans (Science, April 2009)
First ARPANET message sent from UCLA (Charley Kline, Leonard Kleinrock's lab) to SRI; system crashed after 'lo'

sources.title: ARPANET launches the world's first packet-switched wide area computer network

what: Tim Berners-Lee made the first World Wide Web site (info.cern.ch) publicly available from CERN; Web software placed in public domain 1993-04-30
MIT's CTSS MAILBOX let users of the same time-sharing computer leave messages for each other
Ray Tomlinson (BBN) sent the first networked email over ARPANET, introducing user@host addressing

sources.title: Ray Tomlinson sends the first email

what: NLM's MEDLINE online service began interactive searching from remote terminals at medical libraries (55 cities by Feb 1972)
IBM Watson answered open-domain natural-language questions and beat Jeopardy! champions Rutter and Jennings
Sony released the Librie EBR-1000EP in Japan, the first consumer e-reader with an E Ink display.
Amazon launched the Kindle at $399; it reportedly sold out in about five and a half hours.
Nick Sheridon at Xerox PARC built the Gyricon rotating-ball electronic paper (sources say 1974 or 1975; the prototype was a rigid clipboard-like display).
Sony's Librie in Japan was the first consumer product to use an E Ink electronic paper module.

Actuality Systems' Perspecta, a swept-volume display showing a 3D image viewable from all sides, appeared around 2001. Earlier volumetric prototypes were not checked, and a true hologram display is not established.
MIT's Whirlwind computer, operational in 1951, showed real-time text and graphics on a CRT console.
The first SAGE Direction Center (McGuire AFB, NJ) went into regular operation; consoles showed radar-tracked aircraft from computer data. Some sources give 26 June 1958.
E.A. Johnson at the Royal Radar Establishment, Malvern, published a capacitive touch display for computers (air traffic control). Published Oct or Nov 1965.

sources.title: The Royal Air Force and the Invention of the Modern Touchscreen

what: Apple unveiled the multi-touch iPhone; it went on sale in June 2007, making touchscreens a routine consumer interface.

sources.title: Apple Reinvents the Phone with iPhone

what: The US Post Office put a high-speed OCR mail sorter into service at Detroit (Siemens in Germany also reported a mail sorting system in Pforzheim on 1965-05-31).
The Morris worm, released by Robert Tappan Morris, spread across the Internet and disabled many machines. Creeper (1971, BBN, ARPANET) was an earlier experimental self-replicating program.

sources.title: Computer Viruses: How Did It All Start?

what: The Starfish Prime high-altitude nuclear test over the Pacific unexpectedly disrupted electronics in Hawaii, about 1,445 km away.
Bell Labs' Audrey recognized the ten spoken digits from a single speaker.

sources.title: Nervous System: Audrey and the Dragon

what: Apple launched Siri, built into the iPhone 4S, putting voice command in ordinary users' hands.

sources.title: 10 years of Siri: the history of Apple's voice assistant

what: Dragon Systems released Dragon NaturallySpeaking 1.0, the first general-purpose continuous-speech dictation product for PCs. A discrete-speech DragonDictate (1990) is unverified.
Bell Labs' Homer Dudley unveiled the keyboard-operated Voder speech synthesizer at the New York World's Fair.
Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT published ELIZA, a pattern-matching program that held typed conversations in English.
The Georgetown-IBM experiment translated about 49-60 Russian sentences into English on an IBM computer.
The US Air Force's AN/GSQ-16 Automatic Language Translator was installed at Wright-Patterson's Foreign Technology Division for real translation work, and was later replaced by SYSTRAN in 1970.
Colossus Mark 1, built by Tommy Flowers's team, became operational at Bletchley Park against the Lorenz cipher. A working prototype existed by December 1943.

sources.url: https://computinghistory.org.uk/det/6014/The Colossus Mark 1 computer is delivered to Bletchley Park
sources.title: The Colossus Mark 1 computer is delivered to Bletchley Park

what: Christopher Strachey's program on the Ferranti Mark 1 at Manchester generated love letters from templates and word lists.
Lejaren Hiller and Leonard Isaacson used the ILLIAC I at the University of Illinois to compose the Illiac Suite string quartet (sources say 1956 or 1957).
Arthur Samuel published a paper showing a checkers program that learned to play better than its programmer (IBM Journal of R&D).

sources.title: Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers

what: Los Alamos's MANIAC I played a reduced 6x6 chess variant (Los Alamos chess). Deep Blue beat world champion Kasparov in May 1997, which reaches the 'best human level' clause but is not a listed kind.
Christopher Strachey's draughts program first ran on the Ferranti Mark 1 at Manchester in summer 1952, after an earlier failed run at NPL in 1951. Sources vary.

Larry Roberts's MIT PhD thesis 'Machine Perception of Three-Dimensional Solids' showed a computer extracting 3D structure of block objects from camera images (a block-world analysis). Often called the birth of computer vision, though 'first' is contested.

sources.title: Lawrence Roberts Publishes "Machine Perception of Three Dimensional Solids"

what: Persaud and Dodd (Warwick) published an electronic nose using semiconductor transducers to discriminate odours, in Nature.

sources.title: Analysis of discrimination mechanisms in the mammalian olfactory system using a model nose

what: First Unimate robot installed on a General Motors die-casting line in New Jersey (Ternstedt/Inland Fisher Guide plant). Some sources say 1959 or 1960.
Fujitsu Fanuc's robot plant in Japan reported running unattended by robots, making robots, for 16 hours of each working day. Later sources date Fanuc's lights-out operation to 2001.

sources.title: Latest from Japan -- robots making robots

what: Unimation, the first robot-making company (founded 1956 by Devol and Engelberger, Danbury, CT), delivered its first commercial Unimate to GM in 1961.
WABOT-1 completed at Waseda University under Ichiro Kato. It walked on two legs, grasped objects with tactile hands and spoke simple Japanese. Some sources say 1972.

sources.title: Waseda traces 50 years of Waseda humanoid robots development

what: Hiroshi Ishiguro and Kokoro unveiled Geminoid HI-1, a teleoperated android modelled on Ishiguro himself. It is not autonomous, so this is a loose fit.
Electrolux Trilobite, the first commercial robotic vacuum cleaner, went on sale in Sweden (Nov 2001). iRobot's Roomba followed in 2002.

sources.title: Der erste Saugroboter kam nicht von iRobot

what: Savioke's Relay delivery robot went into continuous service at the Aloft Cupertino hotel, carrying items to guests' rooms
Quisisana, the first documented automat (self-service restaurant), opened in Berlin. Horn & Hardart opened the first US Automat in Philadelphia in June 1902.

sources.title: 818 Chestnut Street: Where the Automat Began

what: AIST (Japan) team led by Takanori Shibata unveiled the first-generation Paro baby-seal companion robot, after work begun in 1993
Paro (8th generation, developed 2004) commercialised in Japan as a therapeutic companion robot; sources give 2004 or 2005
W. Grey Walter in Bristol built the Elmer and Elsie tortoise robots (phototaxis, self-recharging); press coverage late 1949
Sony put the first AIBO robot dog on sale in Japan; 3,000 units sold out in about 20 minutes (Guinness says 31 May)
Al-Jazari completed his Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices describing about 50 working mechanical devices incl. automata; much earlier automata (antiquity) exist but not checked

sources.title: Al-Jazari Creates the First Recorded Designs of a Programmable Automaton

what: Knightscope shipped its first K5 autonomous security patrol robot to a customer

UN Panel of Experts reported Turkish STM Kargu-2 drones in Libya programmed to attack targets without a data link ('fire, forget and find'); contested whether autonomous and whether first (earlier ship-defence systems not checked)

sources.title: A UN Report Suggests Libya Saw The First Battlefield Killing By An Autonomous Drone

what: Ford Instrument Co. Rangekeeper, an analog mechanical fire-control computer, judged far superior by US Navy in 1916 trials; first Mark 1 installed on USS Texas

First SAGE direction center went into regular operation, with IBM AN/FSQ-7 computers processing radar data to track aircraft and direct interceptors (closest real analogue; tactical rather than war-planning)
Staples deployed Kiva Systems' fleet of warehouse drive-unit robots, coordinated by control software, at its Chambersburg, PA facility

sources.title: Three Engineers, Hundreds of Robots, One Warehouse

what: Raymond Goertz at Argonne National Laboratory built a master-slave manipulator for handling radioactive material (patent filed 1949; some sources say 1948 design; GE's Payne had a similar 1948 device)
Soviet Lunokhod 1 rover landed on the Moon (Luna 17) and was driven remotely from Earth for about 11 months (earlier flyby/impact probes not checked)
Nature papers showed DNA-based molecular robots (molecular spiders walking programmed origami tracks; DNA assembly line); autonomous DNA walkers date to 2004. No in-body use yet
Chuck Hull filed the stereolithography patent (US 4,575,330, granted 1986-03-11); Kodama filed a similar patent weeks earlier

sources.title: Chuck Hull Invents Stereolithography or 3D Printing and Produces the First Commercial 3D Printer

what: 3D Systems introduced the SLA-1, first commercial stereolithography machine (sources vary 1987 to 1988)

sources.title: First Commercially Successful Stereolithography Machine, Model SLA-1, 1987

what: Cyberware Laboratories released its laser-stripe Head Scanner producing 3D computer images of the human head (touch-probe CMMs earlier, unverified)
Lawrence Sperry flew a Curtiss with gyroscopic autopilot hands-off at the Paris Concours de la Securite en Aeroplane; system developed 1912
Apollo Guidance Computer, designed by MIT Instrumentation Lab, first flew on Apollo 7 (Oct 1968) and guided Apollo 11 to the Moon in 1969 (Gemini computer 1965 not checked)
Ernst Dickmanns' VaMoRs Mercedes van drove itself on an unopened autobahn using cameras and computers (Tsukuba 1977 vehicle was rail- or marker-aided)

sources.title: The Self-Driving Car Story Started Earlier Than You Think

what: Hewitt-Sperry Automatic Airplane flew about 1,000 yards pilotless under gyroscopic control (US Navy test); Kettering Bug tests Sept-Oct 1918
CBS used UNIVAC I on election night to forecast the presidential result; it predicted an Eisenhower landslide (438 EV vs actual 442)

Chile's Project Cybersyn (Stafford Beer, Fernando Flores) sent daily production data from nationalized factories by telex to a central mainframe in Santiago; used by the Allende government, notably in the October 1972 strike
Fair, Isaac & Co. introduced its first credit application scoring system for a small finance company in Louisiana. Whether it ran on a computer at the time is not confirmed.

Operation Match, run by Harvard students through Compatibility Research Inc., matched people from questionnaire answers punched onto cards and run on an IBM computer. The search summary says a London service, St. James Computer Dating Service, began in 1964.

The US Department of Defense began operational use of the computerized adaptive ASVAB (CAT-ASVAB) at Military Entrance Processing Stations in 1996-1997. This is a loose fit: it tests aptitude by computer but does not choose from records.

Mead Data Central launched the LEXIS computerized legal research service commercially, with four big firms as first subscribers. It carried Ohio and New York codes and cases, the US Code and some federal case law.
The LAPD deployed PredPol, a UCLA-developed algorithm for predicting where crime will happen, in its Foothill Division in late 2011. Santa Cruz also began trying it in 2011.

Georgia counties were the first to use punch cards and computer tally machines for voting, per a timeline source. The Votomatic punch-card system was introduced around 1964. The exact county and year are unconfirmed.

sources.title: Balls to Cards: A History of Voting Machines since 1838

what: Ralph Schwitzgebel and his brother Robert, at Harvard, built a system that relayed signals from worn transmitters to a surplus missile-tracking device and displayed participants' positions on a large screen. The start date is uncertain.

Judge Jack Love in New Mexico ordered a Michael Goss radio-frequency ankle transmitter attached to a probation violator for a month. This was radio-based, not GPS; GPS offender monitoring was piloted in Florida in 1997.

sources.title: Let's Stop Using Ankle Bracelets to Monitor Offenders

what: IBM engineer Forrest Parry made the first prototype of a plastic card with magnetic tape, meant as a secure ID card for CIA officials. The year is uncertain.
Tor Sørnes launched the VingCard, the first recodable cardkey lock, using a punched-hole plastic key. A hotel that had suffered burglaries tested it. The date comes from a single source.

The FBI's IAFIS, built by Lockheed Martin, became operational in July 1999. It is not the earliest automated system: the FBI began its automation effort around 1969 and had Rockwell build the first AFIS card readers. I could not confirm that date.

John Daugman was awarded a patent for his automated iris recognition algorithms. Flom and Safir had patented the concept of iris identification in 1986 or 1987. The retina-scanning half of the concept was not covered by my searches.
The FBI's iris recognition overview says the first commercial iris recognition products became available in 1995. Iris ID dates its commercially viable IrisAccess 2200 to 1999.

Woody Bledsoe, Helen Chan and Charles Bisson worked in 1964-65 on semi-automated computer recognition of faces. This was semi-automated; Kanade's 1973 system is sometimes called the first fully automated one.

sources.title: The Secret History of Facial Recognition

what: Pruzansky and Mathews at Bell Labs published early speaker recognition experiments on ten talkers. Doddington at Texas Instruments built a speaker verification system in the early 1970s.

sources.publisher: Gibbon, Handbook of Standards and Resources for Spoken Language Systems
sources.title: Speaker verification

what: LEO I at J. Lyons & Co. ran the first business application, bakery valuations, on 5 September 1951. One source says it first did payroll in November 1951; another says regular payroll began in December 1953. IBM introduced the MT/ST in 1964, which popularised the term word processing.
Westinghouse engineer Jim Sutherland's ECHO IV home computer was operational in his house, running household tasks with keypads and terminals around the home.

sources.title: The ECHO IV Home Computer: 50 Years Later

what: Dee Horton and Lew Hewitt founded Horton Automatics and put the first commercial automatic sliding door on the market. It was mat-actuated; they invented it in 1954. An earlier 1931 Stanley optical door is unconfirmed.
Charney, Fjørtoft and von Neumann ran the first computer weather forecast on ENIAC, published in 1950. The forecast itself may date to 1949.

The Joint Numerical Weather Prediction Unit in Suitland, Maryland, began operational numerical forecasting in May 1955 using a three-level model. The Swedish BESK computer ran routine forecasts from December 1954.

Sidney Pressey at Ohio State University created a mechanical teaching machine that tested students with multiple-choice questions. Skinner's machine followed in 1954, and PLATO began at the University of Illinois around 1960.
MYCIN, a rule-based expert system for diagnosing bacterial infections and recommending antibiotics, developed at Stanford (Shortliffe's doctoral work); never used clinically
Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT published ELIZA (DOCTOR script), a program simulating a Rogerian psychotherapist; a pattern-matching analogue, not a true assessment or therapy system
John Larson, a Berkeley police officer, built the first operational polygraph (cardio-pneumo-psychogram) at Chief August Vollmer's request
Larson used the polygraph in a Berkeley police investigation of dormitory thefts, questioning the residents

sources.title: Larson Constructs the First Modern Polygraph

what: Hans Berger made the first human EEG recording in Jena in 1924 (date of 6 July reported by some sources); he published it in 1929

sources.title: How Hans Berger's quest for telepathy spurred modern brain science

what: Nishimoto, Gallant et al. (UC Berkeley) reconstructed approximate movie clips a subject had watched from fMRI brain activity (Current Biology, Sept 2011); a partial, limited fit to the definition

sources.title: Reconstructing visual experiences from brain activity evoked by natural movies

what: Willett et al. (Stanford, BrainGate) decoded imagined handwriting from motor cortex of a paralysed man into on-screen text at about 90 characters/min (Nature, May 2021)

sources.title: Software turns handwriting thoughts into on-screen text

what: Jacques Vidal at UCLA showed a noninvasive EEG visual-evoked-potential interface letting a user move a cursor through a maze, following his 1973 paper proposing the brain-computer interface
William House and John Doyle in Los Angeles implanted gold-insulated electrodes in the cochleas of two deaf patients
The FDA approved marketing of the 3M/House single-channel cochlear implant for adults in the US

sources.title: Hearing Aid Evolution - A Ride Through History

what: Alois Saliger's Psychophone, an apparatus for teaching during sleep, was introduced (patented 1932 per Wikipedia); 1950s RAND and EEG studies found complex sleep learning ineffective, so only the device, not an effective method, fits

sources.title: A Critical Review of the "Learn-While-You-Sleep" Studies

what: Ivan Sutherland and Bob Sproull demonstrated a computer-driven head-mounted display with head tracking (Sword of Damocles); Heilig's Sensorama (patented 1962) was an earlier non-computer immersive booth
Lucasfilm's Habitat (Farmer, Morningstar et al.) ran in beta on Quantum Link as a graphical multi-user world with avatars; earlier text MUDs (1978) are not confirmed by my searches
Edwin Link built the 'Pilot Maker' trainer in Binghamton, NY (patent application filed 14 April 1929), with pilot controls driving instruments

sources.title: Edwin Link Builds the First Flight Simulator

what: The US Army Air Corps bought six Link Trainers for instrument flight training (year 1934 not confirmed from a full page)
